verses.1: After these things there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.2: Now in Jerusalem there was a pool, called in Hebrew Bethsaida, having five colonnades.
verses.3: In these lay a large number of people who were ill, blind, lame, and paralyzed.
verses.5: One of them was a man who had been ill for thirty-eight years.
verses.6: Seeing him lying there and knowing that he had already been there a long time, Jesus said to him, "Do you want to become well?"
verses.7: The sick man answered him, "Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up. But while I am trying to go, someone else goes down ahead of me."
verses.8: Jesus said to him, "Get up, take up your mat and walk."
verses.9: Immediately the man became well, and he took up his mat and began to walk. Now it was the Sabbath.
verses.10: So the Jews said to the man who had been healed, "It is the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to carry your mat."
verses.11: But he replied, "The one who made me well told me, 'Take up your mat and walk.'"
verses.12: Then they asked him, "Who is the man who said to you, 'Take up your mat and walk'?"
verses.13: But the one who had been healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had slipped away in the crowd that was there.
verses.14: Later Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, "Look, you have become well. Do not sin anymore, or something worse will happen to you."
verses.15: The man went away and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
verses.16: Therefore the Jews began to persecute Jesus because he did these things on the Sabbath.
verses.17: But Jesus said to them, "My Father is working until now, and I also am working."
verses.18: For this reason the Jews tried to kill him even more, because he not only broke the Sabbath, but also called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
verses.19: So Jesus answered them, "Truly, truly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of his own accord unless he sees the Father doing it. For whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
verses.20: For the Father loves the Son and shows him all that he himself does. And greater works than these will he show him, so that you may marvel.
verses.21: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom he will.
verses.22: And the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son,
verses.23: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. He who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent him.
verses.24: "Truly, truly, I say to you, whoever hears my word and believes in him who sent me has eternal life and will not come into judgment, but has passed from death to life.
verses.25: "Truly, truly, I say to you, the hour is coming, and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
verses.26: For just as the Father has life in himself, so he has granted the Son to have life in himself,
verses.27: and he has given him authority to execute judgment, because he is the Son of Man.
verses.28: Do not marvel at this, for the hour is coming when all who are in the tombs will hear his voice
verses.29: and come out, those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment.
verses.30: "I can do nothing on my own. I judge as I hear, and my judgment is just, because I seek not my own will but the will of him who sent me."
verses.31: "If I testify about myself, my testimony is not true,
verses.32: but there is another who testifies about me, and I know that the testimony he gives about me is true.
verses.33: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
verses.34: But I do not receive my testimony from a human being. I say these things so that you may be saved.
verses.35: He was a burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for a while in his light.
verses.36: But I have a testimony greater than that of John. For the works that the Father has given me to accomplish, these very works that I am doing, bear witness that it is the Father who has sent me.
verses.37: And the Father who sent me has himself testified to me. You have neither heard his voice nor seen his form at any time,
verses.38: nor do you have his word abiding in you, because you do not believe him whom he has sent.
verses.39: "You search the Scriptures because you think that in them you have eternal life; and it is they that bear witness about me,
verses.40: yet you refuse to come to me so that you may have life.
verses.41: "I do not receive glory from people,
verses.42: but I know that you do not have the love of God within you.
verses.43: I have come in my Father's name, and you do not receive me. If another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
verses.44: How can you believe, when you accept glory from one another and yet do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
verses.45: "Do not think that I will accuse you before the Father. There is one who accuses you, Moses, on whom you have set your hope.
verses.46: For if you had believed Moses, you would have believed me, for he wrote of me.
verses.47: But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe my words?"

Notes
- v. 4: The original source text is missing verse 4.
- v. 3: "the deep" is not used for "tehom" in this context.
- v. 8: "the Word" is not used for "logos" in this context.
